rules.instruction: When the description lists several distinct kinds of occurrence that one actor must all notify to the same recipient, and the steps that follow depend on which kind occurred: After the notifying task, model an exclusive gateway that classifies which kind of occurrence has been reported. Give it one outgoing branch per kind listed in the description, and let each branch continue with the follow-up stated for that kind. Do not place the later condition gateways directly after the notifying task, because that leaves the classification implicit.
rules.situation: the description lists several distinct kinds of occurrence that one actor must all notify to the same recipient, and the steps that follow depend on which kind occurred

rules.instruction: When the description makes a branch depend on an event together with a status that the affected party must have, for example being insured or a severity threshold that applies only to some parties, so the decision tests both conditions at once: Name the exclusive gateway with a question that states the triggering event and the required status together, using the description's own terms. Make each outgoing flow test that same combined criterion, with one flow for each outcome. Do not name the gateway after only one of the two conditions, and do not leave one condition implicit in the flow labels.
rules.situation: the description makes a branch depend on an event together with a status that the affected party must have, for example being insured or a severity threshold that applies only to some parties, so the decision tests both conditions at once

rules.instruction: When the description lists several kinds of occurrence that the actor must each report, and a different reporting obligation (recipient, deadline, or form) is stated for at least one of those kinds: Model an exclusive gateway after the step in which the actor first reports the occurrence, with one outgoing flow per kind of occurrence, each labeled with that kind's condition in the description's own wording. Place each kind's stated follow-up reporting task (or its end) behind its own flow, labeled with that obligation's wording, so that the deadline, recipient, or form applies only to its kind. Do not place these follow-up reports in an unconditioned sequence, do not join them into one task, and do not connect them with parallel flows.
rules.situation: the description lists several kinds of occurrence that the actor must each report, and a different reporting obligation (recipient, deadline, or form) is stated for at least one of those kinds

rules.instruction: When the description states that a party must notify an external body or insurer about an event under one stated condition, and states a separate notification duty for the same event under a different stated condition, each with its own deadline or recipient: Model each separately stated notification duty as its own task, labelled with the description's notification wording, placed in the branch where its condition holds and after the gateway that tests that condition. Do not let one notification task stand in for a duty with a different condition, and do not leave out a duty whose condition is stated separately.
rules.situation: the description states that a party must notify an external body or insurer about an event under one stated condition, and states a separate notification duty for the same event under a different stated condition, each with its own deadline or recipient

rules.instruction: When the description states that one participant must report several kinds of occurrence, and after that report the kinds differ in their further steps, some requiring a separate follow-up step and others requiring none: Model an exclusive (XOR) gateway directly after the reporting activity. Give it one outgoing flow per kind stated in the description, labeled with the condition that distinguishes that kind. Each flow leads either to the follow-up activity for that kind or to the shared continuation when that kind has no further step. Do not replace this gateway with a user activity that only classifies the occurrence, and do not put the follow-up activities before the gateway.
rules.situation: the description states that one participant must report several kinds of occurrence, and after that report the kinds differ in their further steps, some requiring a separate follow-up step and others requiring none

rules.instruction: When the description states a required action toward a named party (such as an insurer, authority or employer) and attaches to that action a time limit or a list of qualifying criteria: Label the task with a short verb-object phrase that names the required action and the receiving party, in the description's own wording. Keep the time limit and the qualifying criteria out of the label. Do not copy a full list entry or a deadline phrase into the task name.
rules.situation: the description states a required action toward a named party (such as an insurer, authority or employer) and attaches to that action a time limit or a list of qualifying criteria
